title: THE NAMES MISSING FROM THE MANIFEST
deck: A coolant fault will seal the lower decks of the cargo liner Marigold in forty minutes, and the manifest says every one of four hundred and twelve people is already at the boats. Illuminara, a passenger who smelled fresh bread at three in the morning, has to find the people the list cannot see, and then persuade them, on their own terms, that anyone counting them tonight means to bring them out.
shape: Six scenes in forty minutes and a little after: a clean count and a loaf nobody listed; what the ship's doors remember; a cook who will not hand over names; the laundry, where the refusal comes with its own price; a stair, a door and sixty-one voices; and a roll call in the lifeboats.

scenes.title: A Clean Count
paragraphs: *Boat deck, cargo liner Marigold · 03:14, ship-night*

The alarm had been sounding for four minutes and nobody was screaming, which told Illuminara the ship was well run. Passengers came up the stairs in coats over nightclothes. Deck officers moved along the four boat stations ticking names off tablets. Illuminara, cabin 118, stood at the rail with a paper cup of tea she had not finished and listened to the hull. Under her feet a coolant line was breathing out cold, and the white vapour was sinking through the lower decks the way cold water sinks in a bath.

First Officer Idris Kovac stood at the head of boat two with the manifest in one hand and his radio in the other. He read the count aloud to the bosun, steadily, like a man who had trained for exactly this.

**Idris Kovac**  
Four hundred and twelve aboard. Four hundred and twelve at stations. Lower decks seal from the bottom at 03:52, so boats one and two load first.
Illuminara walked over with the tea still in her hand. She had been turning something over since the stairwell.

**Illuminara**  
First Officer, who baked the bread?

**Idris Kovac**  
I'm sorry?

**Illuminara**  
Deck nine, the galley passage. When I came up at ten past three the loaves were still hot. Two hundred rolls, every one scored by hand with a knife. I've walked that passage three nights running and the bread was always there before dawn. Your manifest lists six night galley crew. They're standing at boat two in white jackets. None of them was in that kitchen.

**Idris Kovac**  
The proofing drawers are automatic.

**Illuminara**  
The drawers don't hold a knife.
He did not answer at once. He was not a careless man, and she watched him do the sum and dislike it.

**Idris Kovac**  
Then there may be people I haven't listed. I can't find them in forty minutes. I have four hundred and twelve I can count and every minute spent on a bread knife comes off their boats. I won't turn a boat back for a rumour, and I won't send my ratings down into decks that are about to seal.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not asking you to turn a boat back. I'm asking what else on this ship counts people without asking who they are.
Kovac looked at the manifest as though it had been rude to him. Then he looked at his watch.

**Idris Kovac**  
Three minutes. Engineering, Deck six. Third Engineer Rao has the board.

scenes.title: What the Doors Remember
paragraphs: *Engineering control, Deck 6 · 03:20*
Anika Rao had four screens lit and her sleeves pushed to the elbow. The fault had made a mess of half of them.

Illuminara stood behind her and took the problem apart aloud, because three minutes was not enough to do it quietly. The manifest knew who held a berth. Everything else on the ship knew only what happened to it. The scrubbers had been cycling since the leak began, so the air could not be trusted tonight. The laundry's machines ran themselves, so the water and the power said nothing about hands. She wanted the one record that did not care who you were.

**Illuminara**  
Pressure doors. Every one on the lower decks logs each time it opens. A door doesn't ask who you are, it just opens. Pull the last half hour on Decks eleven and twelve.

**Anika Rao**  
There are cargo trolleys on those decks. Every cycle is going to look like a trolley.

**Illuminara**  
Then subtract the trolleys. They log their own routes. Whatever is left opened for somebody walking.

Rao's hands went to work. Kovac, who had not meant to stay, found that he was reading over her shoulder. The trolley routes came off the log like a coat off a chair, and what stayed was not a scatter. It was a beat. One door on Deck twelve, the aft bunk block, opening and closing every ninety seconds without a miss.

**Anika Rao**  
That's a crowd. It hasn't stopped since the alarm.
On the screen the door went on opening and closing, like something trying a lock. Illuminara watched it for a count of four and did not like how tidy it was.

**Illuminara**  
A crowd bunches. People go to bed at different times and get up at different times. Does that door ever miss a beat?

Rao dragged the log back past the first alarm. Before 03:10 the door had behaved like a door: twice in the last hour, once for a night cleaner and once for a late sleeper, with long gaps between. At 03:10 exactly it had started to keep time, and in the ten minutes since it had not missed once.

**Anika Rao**  
No. Flat as a ruler since 03:10, and nothing like it before.

**Illuminara**  
Then it isn't a crowd. It's the ship.
Rao swore, quietly and with feeling, and dragged the fault table across from the second screen.

**Anika Rao**  
Aft bunk door. The leak's dropping the pressure on one side, so the seal is hunting. It started when the fault started, 03:10.

**Idris Kovac**  
That is six minutes gone on a door with a cold.
Illuminara made herself slow down and think about the corridors instead of the doors. A machine opens a door and has finished. A person walks through, and a corridor has more than one door in it.

**Illuminara**  
People come in pairs. A door, and then the next door along, a few seconds later, which is how long it takes to walk the corridor. Throw out the hunting door and the trolleys, and keep only the pairs.

**Idris Kovac**  
And anything with a badge. My people badge every door they touch.

Rao typed the filter with two fingers and a thumb. It ran for four seconds, which felt very long. The hunting door fell off the screen. So did the trolleys, and so did Kovac's badged crew. What stayed was a scatter of small amber pairs, two or three a minute, drawn along the corridors by the laundry and the aft bunk block, each tick followed by its neighbour at a human pace, and nothing left that looked like a machine.

**Anika Rao**  
Fifty. Maybe seventy. They haven't touched a badge reader all night, and the last ten minutes they've been moving. Whoever they are, they heard the alarm and nobody told them where to go.
Nobody spoke.

**Idris Kovac**  
If they're down there, they're agency labour. Halvard Marine Crewing hires them off my books and I've never signed for one. They have no seats on any sheet, but the seats exist. Boat one is loaded and swung out, and I won't unload it into a panic to save eleven places. It goes at 03:31. The other three boats have fifty-seven empty between them, and past that people sit on the floor. No certificate allows that. It is an emergency breach, and I'll log it as one, with my name under it. What I can't do is send anyone after them. I won't spend a rating on a deck that seals in thirty minutes.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not asking for a rating. I'm asking for the time, and for the last boat to be held.

**Idris Kovac**  
Boat four waits until 03:49. Not a minute past. At 03:49 I lower it whoever is on it, and I'll answer to you and to them for that for the rest of my life.
It was the best answer he had, and she took it as such.

**Illuminara**  
Who would know them?

**Anika Rao**  
Dessa Okafor. Day galley. She's on that deck at all hours and the rota never explains why.

scenes.title: The Cook Who Would Not Give Names
paragraphs: *Galley passage, Deck 9 · 03:27*
Dessa Okafor was not at her boat. She stood at the pass with flour to her elbows, putting loaves into a sack one at a time, and she did not turn when Illuminara came in.

**Dessa Okafor**  
If the Deck-six lot sent you for a count, you can tell them I'm at the boats.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody sent me for a count. And you are at the boats. Somebody answered here for you.

**Dessa Okafor**  
The galley covers for its own.
Illuminara filed that away. The tablets counted voices, and the galley counted hands.

**Illuminara**  
I smelled your bread.
Dessa's hands stopped on the sack.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Not mine. I'm days. I just get here early.

**Illuminara**  
I think there are sixty people on Decks eleven and twelve who didn't get a seat on any sheet, and I think you know where they sleep. The decks seal at 03:52. The first officer is holding boat four until 03:49.
For a moment the passage held only the tick of the cooling ovens.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Do you know what names are to them? A name on a manifest is a name Halvard can find. Last winter a man came down with a clipboard and said it was for their safety. Eight of them had lost their contracts by spring. You want me to hand sixty names to a stranger with the boats loading and the company's name on every door.
Illuminara did not say that this was different. She had no way to know that it was.

**Illuminara**  
No. I don't want the names. I want them out of the ship. How they come, and in what order, and what they ask for first is theirs and yours to say. I can't promise what the first officer will sign. I can ask him in front of you and you can hear what he says.

**Dessa Okafor**  
And if I won't take you down?

**Illuminara**  
Then I'll go down alone and they'll be right not to open for me.
Dessa looked at the sack of bread, and then at the stair. She put the loaf in, pulled the drawstring tight, and slung it onto her back.

**Dessa Okafor**  
They won't come for you. They might come for me. Keep the radio on and keep your mouth shut until Marta speaks.

scenes.title: Sixty-One
paragraphs: *Laundry, Deck 12 · 03:34*

The laundry was warm and wet and very quiet. The machines stood idle, steam still lifting off the pressing tables, and between the dryers, in rows as neat as pews, sat sixty-odd people who had been told by every sign on the ship that this was a place they could stay.
A woman in a grey apron rose from the front row before the stair door had finished swinging. She was perhaps fifty, with forearms like rope, and she kept her eyes on Dessa.

**Marta Szeliga**  
You shouldn't be down here, Dess.

**Dessa Okafor**  
The ship is sealing. Four decks of cold are coming down this stair in twenty minutes, Marta. This is Illuminara. She walked into my galley because of the bread.

**Marta Szeliga**  
We tried the stair at ten past. The reader on the door doesn't know us. It shows red, so we came back where it's warm.
A boy stood up behind her, thin and blue-overalled, with engine grease in the creases of his hands.

**Joss Varga**  
What makes it show green now?

**Illuminara**  
Nothing. I'll hold the door open with my own hands and stand in it until the last of you has gone through. You don't have to come with me. You only have to pass me.

**Marta Szeliga**  
People with a good face have come to count us before.

**Illuminara**  
I know. I'm not going to count you. I don't know your names.
Marta watched her for a long moment, and the room watched Marta.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Sixty-one.

**Illuminara**  
I'm sorry?

**Marta Szeliga**  
Sixty-one of us. I counted at the first bell. I always count. A ship that doesn't know you're aboard is a ship you learn to count on your own.
Illuminara stood very still. She had been through this ship for three nights counting nothing, and sixty-one people had been counting one another the whole time.

**Marta Szeliga**  
I'll take the stair. Not for you. For the boy and for the old men by the dryers. But I want something first, and it isn't yours to give. Dessa, is that radio on the open channel?
Dessa held it up. Out on the boat deck, Kovac's voice came in, flattened by the steel.

**Idris Kovac**  
Marigold, Kovac. I'm listening.

**Marta Szeliga**  
First Officer. Marta Szeliga, laundry, Deck twelve. If we climb, I want every one of us in your log under our own names, in your own hand, before the boat touches the water. Not a number. Not a line that says cargo handling. And nobody from Halvard signs for us.
The channel hissed. They could hear a boat winch somewhere above him, and the rattle of a hundred people shuffling to their stations.

**Idris Kovac**  
If I write that this ship carried sixty-one people who aren't on the owner's sheet, the owner has a bad morning and I have a worse year. Understood. Yes. Every name, in ink. Say them to me one at a time as you come through the door and I'll write them down as you say them.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Then we're coming.

scenes.title: Under Their Own Names
paragraphs: *Stair C and the Deck 10 bulkhead · 03:41*

They went up in a column, Dessa first with the sack of bread on her back and the radio at her shoulder, because Dessa was the one they had agreed to follow. Illuminara went last, then ran to the front when the column bunched at the door.

The reader on the stair door still showed red. She did not touch it. She put her palm flat against the steel and leaned, and the frame took the load as though it had been waiting to. The door swung back, and held. Dessa planted herself beside it with the radio at her mouth.
The first person through was Marta, who stopped on the threshold, looked at the open door and then at Illuminara, and said nothing at all. Then she lifted her chin toward the radio.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Marta Szeliga. Laundry. Aboard.

**Idris Kovac**  
Marta Szeliga, laundry, aboard. Written.

After that it went the way a long line goes when one person has gone first. Forty-one names came out of the dark and into the radio in forty-one different voices. A man in his seventies spelled his surname twice because he had never heard anyone ask. A girl in a sleep shirt gave hers like a dare. Joss said his in a voice that cracked and then gave his mother's too, and Kovac wrote them both and read them back.

**Idris Kovac**  
First nineteen to boat two. Next nineteen to boat three. The rest to boat four, and boat four goes at 03:49 whoever is aboard. Two of my ratings are at the stair head above the seal. Above the seal the deck is mine to spend.
At 03:45, with nineteen still below, the Deck ten bulkhead began to close.

The fault had gone faster than the log said. The door began its slow travel, a hand's breadth a second, and the cold came up through it like a held breath. Illuminara got her shoulder to the frame. She could hold one door, and had been counting on that, and she knew it was the only thing she could do alone tonight. Someone had to walk through it of their own accord, and she could not carry them.

**Illuminara**  
Marta, how many left?

**Marta Szeliga**  
Nineteen.

**Illuminara**  
Then count them out.

Marta counted them out loud. The numbers came one at a time, in the voice of a woman who had done it all her life without anyone asking. The frame bit into Illuminara's shoulder. The cold crept up her wrist. Joss, near the end, missed the top rung of the service ladder and went down hard on his ankle, and a stranger and an old man took his arms between them and carried him through. A woman from the dry room caught her hand on a hot steam pipe going past and bit down on the cry.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Sixty.

There was one more. Marta reached back through the gap for her, and the door kept coming, and the last cook ran the final metres with a bread knife still in her hand because she had forgotten to put it down.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Sixty-one.
Above the seal two ratings in white jackets were already at the stair head with their hands out. They took Joss between them and ran, and Dessa ran after them with the sack bouncing on her back.

Illuminara let go. The bulkhead closed on the empty stair with a sound like a vault, and she stood with her arm hanging, shaking in a way that was nothing to do with the cold, and felt something she could not at first name. It was a plain, steady happiness, as if somebody had lit a stove in a cold house.

scenes.title: Roll
paragraphs: *Lifeboat 4, one mile off Marigold · 04:06*

Boat two had gone down at 03:45 and boat three at 03:47, both full. Boat one had left at 03:31 with eleven seats empty, because a loaded boat swung out over black water was not something Kovac would unload to save them. Boat four went at 03:49 with a hundred and twenty-four aboard for a hundred and twenty seats, four of them on the floorboards, and the last of the sixty-one came over the gunwale as the falls took the weight. It was crowded, and it was four over the boat's certificate. Kovac had written the breach into the log himself, with the time and the reason, and would answer for it.

Joss lay across two thwarts with his ankle strapped and his head in his mother's lap. The woman who had burned her hand held it in the sea-wet sleeve of a coat that wasn't hers. Dessa sat in the stern with the sack open between her knees.
Kovac sat in the bow with the log open on his knee. The page was written close, in blue ink, line after line.

**Idris Kovac**  
Halvard Marine Crewing has just answered my report. They say they have no record of any workers on this vessel beyond the listed crew. They say the entry I have made is an error, and that the log is to be surrendered to their marine superintendent when we land.

**Marta Szeliga**  
And what does your book say?

**Idris Kovac**  
That it's right, and so are you. A ship's log is the master's until the harbour authority asks for it, and Halvard is not the harbour authority. Past that, I'll take my instructions from the people it's about.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Then the first one is this. Nobody from Halvard opens that book. At landfall it goes to the port officer, out of your hand, with Dessa standing beside you. Not by radio, not by courier, not through the superintendent.

**Idris Kovac**  
Written.

**Marta Szeliga**  
The second. Anyone who doesn't want their name on a copy that leaves your hands says so tonight, and you strike it in front of them. The book keeps every name.

**Idris Kovac**  
The book keeps every name, and a copy is struck on request. Agreed on both. Now I'm going to read it, and I'd like each of you to say whether I've got you.

He read slowly. He read the names as if he were laying them down one at a time on a table. Marta Szeliga. Joss Varga. A name came up and a voice answered it out of the dark of the boat, and then another.

**Idris Kovac**  
Esperanza Oyelaran.

**Esperanza Oyelaran**  
Here. Leave me off the copy.

Kovac ruled a short line in the margin beside her name and wrote *struck from the copy, at her request*, and went on. Tomasz Brandt. Here. Here. Here. Some said it quietly and some like an argument. It took eleven minutes. He did not skip a name and nobody asked him to.

**Idris Kovac**  
Sixty-one.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Here.
Four hundred and seventy-three people had gone off the Marigold, and every one of them was in a boat.

Behind them the Marigold stood black against the first grey of the east. The sealing was going on in order, deck by deck from the bottom, and the lights went out in rows like a long street being shut for the night. There was no one in any of them.
Dessa passed the sack down the length of the boat. One loaf, then another, each with a knife-scored crown, travelled hand to hand across the cold until every person who wanted one had one.
Illuminara took hers and held it in her good hand. It was still warm.

critic_line: Illuminara finds the sixty-one people the manifest cannot see, listens when they refuse rescue on surveillance terms, and helps them leave under conditions they freely set; Kovac accepts an honest emergency breach and every one of 473 people reaches a boat while injury, retaliation and accountability remain real.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1; exact equal 50/50 mean of two independent source-bound final reader judgments.
shared_strengths: Strong ticking-clock premise, a clever bread clue, and a humane payoff where the hidden workers set terms and are named in the log. Dialogue-heavy and brisk. The door-log deduction runs a little technical and tidy, and the resolution comes easily, but the emotional beats land.

A tense rescue mystery becomes a humane argument about visibility, consent, and institutional responsibility. The dialogue is purposeful, the bread-and-names motifs land emotionally, and the characters earn the hopeful ending. Some technical deduction and the extended post-rescue negotiation feel over-explicit, but the moral stakes and countdown should carry most readers through.
shared_reservations: Illuminara took the problem apart aloud, because three minutes was not enough to do it quietly. The manifest knew who held a berth. Everything else on the ship knew only what happened to it.
The second. Anyone who doesn't want their name on a copy that leaves your hands says so tonight, and you strike it in front of them.

translation_sl.title: IMENA, KI MANJKAJO NA MANIFESTU
translation_sl.deck: Okvara hladilnega sistema bo v štiridesetih minutah zapečatila spodnje palube tovorne ladje Marigold, manifest pa pravi, da je vseh štiristo dvanajst ljudi že pri čolnih. Illuminara, potnica, ki je ob treh zjutraj zavohala svež kruh, mora najti ljudi, ki jih seznam ne vidi, in jih nato pod njihovimi pogoji prepričati, da jih želi vsakdo, ki jih nocoj šteje, spraviti ven.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v štiridesetih minutah in še malo zatem: urejen seštevek in hlebec, ki ga ni nihče vpisal; česa se spominjajo ladijska vrata; kuharica, ki ne bo izročila imen; pralnica, kjer ima zavrnitev svojo ceno; stopnišče, vrata in enainšestdeset glasov; ter poimensko preverjanje v rešilnih čolnih.

scenes.title: Urejen seštevek
paragraphs: *Paluba s čolni, tovorna ladja Marigold · 03:14, ladijska noč*

Alarm je tulil že štiri minute, pa nihče ni kričal, kar je Illuminari povedalo, da je ladja dobro vodena. Potniki so prihajali po stopnicah v plaščih čez nočna oblačila. Palubni častniki so se pomikali ob štirih postajah za čolne in na tablicah odkljukavali imena. Illuminara iz kabine 118 je stala ob ograji s papirnatim lončkom nedopitega čaja in poslušala trup. Pod njenimi stopali je hladilna cev izdihovala mraz, bela para pa se je spuščala skozi spodnje palube tako, kakor se hladna voda v kadi potopi.
Prvi častnik Idris Kovac je stal na čelu drugega čolna z manifestom v eni roki in radijsko postajo v drugi. Število je glasno prebral bocmanu, mirno, kakor človek, ki se je uril prav za to.

**Idris Kovac**  
Štiristo dvanajst na krovu. Štiristo dvanajst na zbirnih mestih. Spodnje palube se od spodaj navzgor zaprejo ob 03:52, zato se prva vkrcata čolna ena in dve.
Illuminara je stopila k njemu, še vedno s čajem v roki. Že od stopnišča je nekaj premlevala.

**Illuminara**  
Prvi častnik, kdo je spekel kruh?

**Idris Kovac**  
Prosim?

**Illuminara**  
Deveta paluba, prehod pri kuhinji. Ko sem se deset čez tri vzpenjala, so bili hlebci še vroči. Dvesto žemelj, vsaka ročno zarezana z nožem. Tri noči zapored sem šla po tem prehodu in kruh je bil vedno tam pred zoro. Vaš manifest navaja šest članov nočne kuhinjske izmene. V belih jopičih stojijo pri drugem čolnu. Nihče od njih ni bil v tisti kuhinji.

**Idris Kovac**  
Vzhajalne omare so avtomatske.

**Illuminara**  
Omare ne držijo noža.
Ni odgovoril takoj. Ni bil malomaren človek in opazovala ga je, kako je opravil račun in mu rezultat ni bil všeč.

**Idris Kovac**  
Potem so morda na ladji ljudje, ki jih nisem vpisal. V štiridesetih minutah jih ne morem najti. Imam štiristo dvanajst ljudi, ki jih lahko preštejem, in vsaka minuta za iskanje krušnega noža gre na račun njihovih čolnov. Čolna ne bom obračal nazaj zaradi govorice in svojih mornarjev ne bom pošiljal na palube, ki se bodo kmalu zapečatile.

**Illuminara**  
Ne prosim vas, da obrnete čoln. Sprašujem, kaj drugega na tej ladji šteje ljudi, ne da bi vprašalo, kdo so.
Kovac je pogledal manifest, kakor da je bil do njega nesramen. Nato je pogledal uro.

**Idris Kovac**  
Tri minute. Strojnica na šesti palubi. Pri nadzorni plošči je tretja strojnica Rao.

scenes.title: Česa se spominjajo vrata
paragraphs: *Nadzorna soba strojnice, 6. paluba · 03:20*
Anika Rao je imela prižgane štiri zaslone in rokave zavihane do komolcev. Okvara je polovico zaslonov spremenila v zmedo.

Illuminara je stala za njo in težavo razstavljala na glas, saj tri minute niso bile dovolj za tiho razmišljanje. Manifest je vedel, kdo ima ležišče. Vse drugo na ladji je vedelo le, kaj se mu je zgodilo. Čistilniki zraka so delovali od začetka puščanja, zato zraku nocoj ni bilo mogoče zaupati. Stroji v pralnici so delovali sami, zato voda in elektrika nista povedali ničesar o rokah. Hotela je edini zapis, ki mu je bilo vseeno, kdo si.

**Illuminara**  
Tlačna vrata. Vsaka na spodnjih palubah zabeležijo vsako odpiranje. Vrata ne vprašajo, kdo si, samo odprejo se. Prikažite zadnje pol ure na enajsti in dvanajsti palubi.

**Anika Rao**  
Na teh palubah so tovorni vozički. Vsak cikel bo videti kot voziček.

**Illuminara**  
Potem odštejte vozičke. Svoje poti beležijo sami. Kar ostane, se je odprlo za nekoga, ki je hodil.

Raove roke so začele delati. Kovac, ki ni nameraval ostati, je ugotovil, da bere čez njeno ramo. Poti vozičkov so zdrsnile z dnevnika kakor plašč s stola, kar je ostalo, pa ni bil raztresen vzorec. Bil je ritem. Ena vrata na dvanajsti palubi, pri zadnjem spalnem bloku, so se brez izpuščenega utripa odpirala in zapirala vsakih devetdeset sekund.

**Anika Rao**  
To je množica. Od alarma se ni ustavilo.
Na zaslonu so se vrata še naprej odpirala in zapirala, kakor da nekaj preizkuša ključavnico. Illuminara jih je opazovala štiri cikle in ni ji bilo všeč, kako urejen je bil vzorec.

**Illuminara**  
Množica se zgosti. Ljudje hodijo spat ob različnih urah in vstajajo ob različnih urah. Ali ta vrata sploh kdaj izpustijo utrip?

Rao je dnevnik potegnila nazaj pred prvi alarm. Pred 03:10 so se vrata vedla kot vrata: dvakrat v zadnji uri, enkrat za nočnega čistilca in enkrat za poznega spalca, z dolgimi premori vmes. Natanko ob 03:10 so začela meriti čas in v desetih minutah zatem niso niti enkrat izpustila utripa.

**Anika Rao**  
Ne. Od 03:10 ravno kot ravnilo, prej pa nič podobnega.

**Illuminara**  
Potem to ni množica. To je ladja.
Rao je tiho in čustveno zaklela ter z drugega zaslona povlekla tabelo okvar.

**Anika Rao**  
Vrata zadnjega spalnega bloka. Puščanje znižuje tlak na eni strani, zato tesnilo niha. Začelo se je z okvaro, ob 03:10.

**Idris Kovac**  
To je šest minut, izgubljenih za vrata, ki so prehlajena.
Illuminara se je prisilila upočasniti in razmišljati o hodnikih namesto o vratih. Stroj odpre vrata in je končal. Človek gre skoznje, hodnik pa ima več kakor ena vrata.

**Illuminara**  
Ljudje prihajajo v parih. Ena vrata, nato nekaj sekund pozneje naslednja ob hodniku, kolikor traja, da ga prehodiš. Izločite nihajoča vrata in vozičke ter obdržite le pare.

**Idris Kovac**  
In vse s službeno priponko. Moji ljudje jo prislonijo pri vsakih vratih, ki se jih dotaknejo.

Rao je filter vtipkala z dvema prstoma in palcem. Izvajal se je štiri sekunde, kar se je zdelo zelo dolgo. Nihajoča vrata so izginila z zaslona. Prav tako vozički in Kovčeva posadka s priponkami. Ostal je raztresen vzorec drobnih jantarnih parov, dva ali trije na minuto, razporejenih po hodnikih pri pralnici in zadnjem spalnem bloku; vsakemu tiku je pri človeški hitrosti sledil sosednji, nič od preostalega pa ni bilo podobno stroju.

**Anika Rao**  
Petdeset. Morda sedemdeset. Vso noč se niso dotaknili čitalnika priponk, zadnjih deset minut pa se premikajo. Kdor koli so, slišali so alarm in nihče jim ni povedal, kam naj gredo.
Nihče ni spregovoril.

**Idris Kovac**  
Če so spodaj, so agencijski delavci. Halvard Marine Crewing jih zaposluje mimo mojih evidenc in za nobenega nisem podpisal. Na nobenem seznamu nimajo sedežev, a sedeži obstajajo. Prvi čoln je naložen in zanihan navzven in ne bom ga raztovoril v paniko, da bi rešil enajst mest. Odhaja ob 03:31. V preostalih treh čolnih je skupaj sedeminpetdeset praznih mest, čez to pa ljudje sedijo na tleh. Noben certifikat tega ne dovoljuje. To je kršitev v sili in tako jo bom zapisal, s svojim imenom pod njo. Ne morem pa nikogar poslati ponje. Mornarja ne bom porabil na palubi, ki se bo zaprla čez trideset minut.

**Illuminara**  
Ne prosim za mornarja. Prosim za čas in za to, da zadržite zadnji čoln.

**Idris Kovac**  
Četrti čoln čaka do 03:49. Niti minute dlje. Ob 03:49 ga spustim, kdor koli bo na njem, in za to bom vam in njim odgovarjal do konca svojega življenja.
To je bil njegov najboljši odgovor in sprejela ga je kot takega.

**Illuminara**  
Kdo bi jih poznal?

**Anika Rao**  
Dessa Okafor. Dnevna kuhinjska izmena. Na tej palubi je ob vseh urah, razpored pa nikoli ne pojasni, zakaj.

scenes.title: Kuharica, ki ni hotela izročiti imen
paragraphs: *Prehod pri kuhinji, 9. paluba · 03:27*
Dessa Okafor ni bila pri svojem čolnu. Stala je pri pultu z moko do komolcev in hlebce enega za drugim zlagala v vrečo, ko je Illuminara vstopila, pa se ni obrnila.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Če vas je ekipa s šeste palube poslala po število, jim lahko poveste, da sem pri čolnih.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče me ni poslal po število. In vi ste pri čolnih. Nekdo je tukaj odgovoril namesto vas.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Kuhinja krije svoje.
Illuminara si je to zapomnila. Tablice so štele glasove, kuhinja pa roke.

**Illuminara**  
Zavohala sem vaš kruh.
Dessine roke so obstale na vreči.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Ni moj. Delam podnevi. Samo zgodaj pridem.

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da je na enajsti in dvanajsti palubi šestdeset ljudi, ki niso dobili sedeža na nobenem seznamu, in mislim, da veste, kje spijo. Palube se zaprejo ob 03:52. Prvi častnik zadržuje četrti čoln do 03:49.
Za trenutek je v prehodu ostalo le tiktakanje peči, ki so se hladile.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Veste, kaj so zanje imena? Ime na manifestu je ime, ki ga Halvard lahko najde. Prejšnjo zimo je prišel dol moški z mapo in rekel, da gre za njihovo varnost. Do pomladi jih je osem izgubilo pogodbe. Vi pa želite, da šestdeset imen izročim neznanki, medtem ko se polnijo čolni in je ime podjetja na vsakih vratih.
Illuminara ni rekla, da je tokrat drugače. Ni mogla vedeti, ali je.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Nočem imen. Hočem jih spraviti z ladje. Kako pridejo, v kakšnem vrstnem redu in kaj najprej zahtevajo, morajo povedati oni in vi. Ne morem obljubiti, kaj bo prvi častnik podpisal. Lahko ga vprašam pred vami in lahko slišite, kaj bo rekel.

**Dessa Okafor**  
In če vas nočem peljati dol?

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom šla dol sama in prav bodo imeli, če mi ne odprejo.
Dessa je pogledala vrečo kruha, nato stopnišče. Vanjo je položila hlebec, zategnila vrvico in si vrečo oprtala na hrbet.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Za vas ne bodo prišli. Zame morda bodo. Pustite radijsko zvezo odprto in bodite tiho, dokler ne spregovori Marta.

scenes.title: Enainšestdeset
paragraphs: *Pralnica, 12. paluba · 03:34*

Pralnica je bila topla, mokra in zelo tiha. Stroji so mirovali, para se je še dvigala s stiskalnih miz, med sušilniki pa je v vrstah, urejenih kot cerkvene klopi, sedelo nekaj več kot šestdeset ljudi, ki jim je vsak znak na ladji povedal, da lahko ostanejo tukaj.
Še preden so se stopniščna vrata nehala nihati, je iz prve vrste vstala ženska v sivem predpasniku. Morda je imela petdeset let, podlahti kakor vrvi, oči pa je držala na Dessi.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Ne bi smela biti tukaj spodaj, Dess.

**Dessa Okafor**  
Ladja se zapira. Čez dvajset minut bodo po teh stopnicah prišle štiri palube mraza, Marta. To je Illuminara. Zaradi kruha je vstopila v mojo kuhinjo.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Ob deset čez smo poskusili po stopnicah. Čitalnik na vratih nas ne pozna. Pokaže rdeče, zato smo se vrnili tja, kjer je toplo.
Za njo je vstal fant, suh in v modrem delovnem kombinezonu, z mastjo iz strojnice v gubah rok.

**Joss Varga**  
Zakaj bo zdaj pokazalo zeleno?

**Illuminara**  
Zaradi ničesar. Vrata bom držala odprta z lastnimi rokami in stala v njih, dokler ne bo šel skozi zadnji med vami. Ni vam treba iti z mano. Samo mimo mene morate.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Ljudje s prijaznim obrazom so nas že prišli štet.

**Illuminara**  
Vem. Ne bom vas štela. Ne poznam vaših imen.
Marta jo je dolgo opazovala in soba je opazovala Marto.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Enainšestdeset.

**Illuminara**  
Prosim?

**Marta Szeliga**  
Enainšestdeset nas je. Preštela sem ob prvem zvoncu. Vedno štejem. Ko ladja ne ve, da si na krovu, se naučiš šteti sam.
Illuminara je stala povsem pri miru. Tri noči je hodila po tej ladji, ne da bi kar koli štela, enainšestdeset ljudi pa je ves čas štelo drug drugega.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Šla bom po stopnicah. Ne zaradi vas. Zaradi fanta in starih moških pri sušilnikih. Toda najprej nekaj hočem, pa tega ne morete dati vi. Dessa, je radijska postaja na odprtem kanalu?
Dessa jo je dvignila. Zunaj na palubi s čolni se je oglasil Kovčev glas, sploščen zaradi jekla.

**Idris Kovac**  
Marigold, Kovac. Poslušam.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Prvi častnik. Marta Szeliga, pralnica, dvanajsta paluba. Če se povzpnemo, hočem, da ste vsakega izmed nas zapisali v svoj dnevnik z našimi pravimi imeni, z lastno roko, še preden se čoln dotakne vode. Ne številke. Ne vrstice, ki pravi pretovor. In nihče iz Halvarda ne podpisuje za nas.
Kanal je zašumel. Nekje nad njim so slišali vitel čolna in ropot stotih ljudi, ki so se pomikali na zbirna mesta.

**Idris Kovac**  
Če zapišem, da je ta ladja prevažala enainšestdeset ljudi, ki jih ni na lastnikovem seznamu, bo imel lastnik slabo jutro, jaz pa slabše leto. Razumem. Da. Vsako ime, s črnilom. Povejte mi jih drugega za drugim, ko pridete skozi vrata, in zapisal jih bom tako, kot jih izgovorite.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Potem prihajamo.

scenes.title: Pod lastnimi imeni
paragraphs: *Stopnišče C in pregrada na 10. palubi · 03:41*

Vzpenjali so se v koloni, prva Dessa z vrečo kruha na hrbtu in radijsko postajo ob ramenu, ker so se dogovorili, da bodo sledili njej. Illuminara je šla zadnja, nato stekla naprej, ko se je kolona zgostila pri vratih.

Čitalnik pri stopniščnih vratih je še vedno kazal rdeče. Ni se ga dotaknila. Dlan je plosko pritisnila ob jeklo in se naslonila, okvir pa je prevzel obremenitev, kakor da je čakal nanjo. Vrata so zanihala nazaj in obstala. Dessa se je postavila poleg njih z radijsko postajo pri ustih.
Prva je šla skozi Marta, ki se je ustavila na pragu, pogledala odprta vrata in nato Illuminari ter ni rekla prav nič. Nato je dvignila brado proti radijski postaji.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Marta Szeliga. Pralnica. Na krovu.

**Idris Kovac**  
Marta Szeliga, pralnica, na krovu. Zapisano.

Potem je šlo tako, kot gre dolga vrsta, ko je prvi človek že šel. Iz teme je v radijsko postajo v enainštiridesetih različnih glasovih prišlo enainštirideset imen. Moški v sedemdesetih je svoj priimek črkoval dvakrat, ker ga še nihče ni vprašal. Dekle v spalni srajci je svojega izgovorilo kakor izziv. Joss je svojega povedal z glasom, ki mu je počil, nato še materinega, Kovac pa je oba zapisal in ponovil.

**Idris Kovac**  
Prvih devetnajst v drugi čoln. Naslednjih devetnajst v tretjega. Ostali v četrtega in četrti odide ob 03:49, kdor koli bo na krovu. Dva moja mornarja sta na vrhu stopnic nad zaporo. Nad zaporo je paluba moja, da jo porabim.
Ob 03:45, ko jih je bilo devetnajst še spodaj, se je pregrada na deseti palubi začela zapirati.

Okvara je napredovala hitreje, kot je govoril dnevnik. Vrata so se začela počasi pomikati, za širino dlani na sekundo, mraz pa je skoznje prihajal navzgor kot zadržan dih. Illuminara je prislonila ramo k okvirju. Lahko je držala ena vrata in na to je računala, vedela pa je, da je to nocoj edino, kar lahko stori sama. Nekdo je moral skoznje stopiti po svoji volji in ona ga ni mogla nesti.

**Illuminara**  
Marta, koliko jih je ostalo?

**Marta Szeliga**  
Devetnajst.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jih preštejte ven.

Marta jih je glasno štela. Številke so prihajale druga za drugo v glasu ženske, ki je to počela vse življenje, ne da bi jo kdor koli prosil. Okvir se je zarezal Illuminari v ramo. Mraz ji je lezel po zapestju. Joss, skoraj na koncu, je zgrešil vrhnjo prečko servisne lestve in trdo padel na gleženj, neznanec in starec pa sta ga prijela pod roke in odnesla skozi. Ženska iz sušilnice se je pri prehodu z roko ujela ob vročo parno cev in zadržala krik.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Šestdeset.
Ostala je še ena. Marta je skozi režo segla ponjo, vrata so se še naprej pomikala, zadnja kuharica pa je zadnje metre pretekla s krušnim nožem še vedno v roki, ker ga je pozabila odložiti.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Enainšestdeset.
Nad zaporo sta pri vrhu stopnic že čakala dva mornarja v belih jopičih z iztegnjenimi rokami. Medse sta vzela Jossa in stekla, Dessa pa za njima z vrečo, ki ji je poskakovala na hrbtu.

Illuminara je popustila. Pregrada se je za praznim stopniščem zaprla z zvokom bančnega trezorja, ona pa je stala z visečo roko in se tresla zaradi nečesa, kar ni imelo nič opraviti z mrazom, ter čutila nekaj, česar sprva ni znala poimenovati. Bila je preprosta, trdna sreča, kakor da bi nekdo zakuril peč v mrzli hiši.

scenes.title: Poimensko preverjanje
paragraphs: *Rešilni čoln 4, miljo od Marigolda · 04:06*

Drugi čoln so spustili ob 03:45 in tretjega ob 03:47, oba polna. Prvi čoln je odšel ob 03:31 z enajstimi praznimi sedeži, ker Kovac naloženega čolna, zanihanega nad črno vodo, ni nameraval raztovoriti, da bi jih rešil. Četrti čoln je odšel ob 03:49 s sto štiriindvajsetimi ljudmi za sto dvajset sedežev, štirje so sedeli na podnicah, zadnji izmed enainšestdesetih pa je prišel čez bok, ko so škripci prevzeli težo. Bilo je tesno in za štiri ljudi so presegli certifikat čolna. Kovac je kršitev sam vpisal v dnevnik, skupaj s časom in razlogom, in zanjo bo odgovarjal.

Joss je ležal čez dve klopi z opornico na gležnju in glavo v materinem naročju. Ženska, ki si je opekla roko, jo je držala v z morsko vodo premočenem rokavu plašča, ki ni bil njen. Dessa je sedela na krmi z odprto vrečo med koleni.
Kovac je sedel na premcu z odprtim dnevnikom na kolenu. Stran je bila gosto popisana z vrstico za vrstico modrega črnila.

**Idris Kovac**  
Halvard Marine Crewing je pravkar odgovoril na moje poročilo. Pravijo, da nimajo evidence o delavcih na tem plovilu razen navedene posadke. Pravijo, da je moj vpis napaka in da moram dnevnik ob pristanku izročiti njihovemu pomorskemu nadzorniku.

**Marta Szeliga**  
In kaj pravi vaša knjiga?

**Idris Kovac**  
Da ima prav in vi tudi. Ladijski dnevnik je kapitanov, dokler ga ne zahteva pristaniška oblast, Halvard pa ni pristaniška oblast. Odtlej bom navodila sprejemal od ljudi, ki jih zadeva.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Potem je prvo navodilo tole. Nihče iz Halvarda ne odpre te knjige. Ob pristanku gre pristaniškemu uradniku, neposredno iz vaših rok, z Desso ob vas. Ne po radijski zvezi, ne s kurirjem, ne prek nadzornika.

**Idris Kovac**  
Zapisano.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Drugo. Kdor ne želi svojega imena na kopiji, ki zapusti vaše roke, naj to pove nocoj in ga pred njim prečrtajte. Knjiga obdrži vsa imena.

**Idris Kovac**  
Knjiga obdrži vsa imena, na zahtevo pa je ime prečrtano na kopiji. Oboje dogovorjeno. Zdaj bom seznam prebral in rad bi, da vsak pove, ali sem ga pravilno zapisal.
Bral je počasi. Imena je izgovarjal, kakor da jih drugega za drugim polaga na mizo. Marta Szeliga. Joss Varga. Ime se je oglasilo in glas iz teme čolna je odgovoril nanj, nato še naslednji.

**Idris Kovac**  
Esperanza Oyelaran.

**Esperanza Oyelaran**  
Tukaj. Mene izpustite s kopije.

Kovac je ob njenem imenu v rob potegnil kratko črto in zapisal *na njeno zahtevo prečrtano na kopiji*, nato nadaljeval. Tomasz Brandt. Tukaj. Tukaj. Tukaj. Nekateri so odgovorili tiho, drugi kakor v prepiru. Trajalo je enajst minut. Nobenega imena ni izpustil in nihče ga ni prosil, naj ga.

**Idris Kovac**  
Enainšestdeset.

**Marta Szeliga**  
Tukaj.
Z ladje Marigold je odšlo štiristo triinsedemdeset ljudi in prav vsak je bil v čolnu.

Za njimi je Marigold črn stal pred prvo sivino vzhoda. Palube so se urejeno zapirale, druga za drugo od spodaj navzgor, luči pa so ugašale v vrstah kakor dolga ulica, ki jo zapirajo za noč. V nobeni ni bilo nikogar.
Dessa je vrečo podala vzdolž čolna. Hlebec za hlebcem, vsak s krono, zarezano z nožem, je potoval iz rok v roke skozi mraz, dokler ga ni dobil vsak, ki ga je želel.
Illuminara je vzela svojega in ga držala v zdravi roki. Še vedno je bil topel.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara najde enainšestdeset ljudi, ki jih manifest ne vidi, prisluhne, ko zavrnejo reševanje pod pogoji nadzora, in jim pomaga oditi pod pogoji, ki jih svobodno določijo sami; Kovac sprejme pošteno evidentirano kršitev v sili in vseh 473 ljudi doseže čoln, medtem ko poškodbe, povračilni ukrepi in odgovornost ostanejo resnični.
